[[File:Himekoso-jinja, torii.jpg|thumb|220px|{{center|Torii Gate}}]]

'''Himekoso Shrine''' (ひめこそじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Higashinari-ku, Osaka|en|Higashinari-ku, Osaka|qid=Q985701|lt=Higashinari-ku|1=Higashinari-ku, Osaka}}, {{ill|Osaka|en|Osaka|qid=Q35765|lt=Osaka City|1=Osaka}}. The shrine was formerly classified as a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度}} and is a proposed site of the {{ill|Shikinai Myōjin-taisha|ja|摂津国東生郡 比売許曽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai Myōjin-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} (another proposed site is the auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Kōzu-gū|en|Kōzu-gū|qid=Q11671792|lt=Kōzu-gū|1=Kōzu-gū}}).

== Enshrined Deities ==
* Primary deity: {{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|シタテルヒメ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|qq=}}
* Other Deities: {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|en|Ajisukitakahikone|qid=Q506610|lt=Ajisukitakahikone|1=Ajisukitakahikone}}, {{ill|Ōhashi-no-Mikoto|ja|大小橋命|1=Ōbashi no Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōhashi-no-Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōbashi no Mikoto|qq=}}, {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|qid=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku|1=Emperor Nintoku}}, {{ill|Tachibana Toyohime|ja|橘豊日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Toyohime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, in the 2nd year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin|1=Emperor Suinin}} in July, at Akumeyama (あくめやま, presently the elevated area of {{ill|Tennōji-ku, Osaka|en|Tennōji-ku, Osaka|qid=Q490592|lt=Tennoji Ward|1=Tennōji-ku, Osaka}} and {{ill|Kobashicho|ja|小橋町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kobashicho|1=obasechou|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97376559}}), the deity {{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|シタテルヒメ|lt=Lower Illumination Hime|lt_ja=下照比売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|qq=}} was enshrined,<ref name="Himekoso Shrine">[https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/higashinari/page/0000588014.html {{ill|Higashinari Ward Homepage|ja|東成区ホームページ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashinari Ward Homepage|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} Himekoso Shrine]</ref> and it is said that the shrine was originally called {{ill|Takatsutenjin|ja|高津天神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takatsutenjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. It is further said that a shrine building was constructed during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kenzō|en|Emperor Kenzō|qid=Q360966|lt=Emperor Kenzō|1=Emperor Kenzō}}.

In the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}, it is recorded that {{ill|Agaru Himekami|ja|阿加流比売神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agaru Himekami|1=Akaruhime-no-Kami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q555212}} from {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|qid=Q28456|lt=Silla|1=Silla}} came to sit at the shrine of {{ill|Himegoso Shrine|ja|比売碁曽の社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Himegoso Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in {{ill|Namba|en|Namba|qid=Q1075406|lt=Namba|1=Namba}}, and a similar account is found in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}. However, in the {{ill|Engi Shiki Deity List|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi Shiki Deity List|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, the Lower Illumination Shrine is identified as Himekoso Shrine,<ref name="Himekoso">[https://kotobank.jp/word/%E6%AF%94%E5%A3%B2%E8%A8%B1%E6%9B%BE%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE-1400435#goog_rewarded Kotobank - Himekoso Shrine]</ref> while the shrine enshrining {{ill|Agaru Hime|ja|阿加流比売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agaru Hime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – {{ill|Akatome Hime Shrine|ja|赤留比売神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akatome Hime Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – is recorded as being in {{ill|Sumiyoshi District|ja|住吉郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sumiyoshi District|1=Sumiyoshi district|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10885872}}.

During the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian Period|1=Heian period}}, the {{ill|Engi Shiki Deity List|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi Shiki Deity List|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}} lists it under {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|lt=Myōjin Taisha|lt_ja=名神大|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myoujin Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Myōjin Taisha|qid=Q9610964}}, and it is recorded that offerings made at the Niiname-sai were received there.

During the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|en|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|qid=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō Era|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)}} (1573 – 1592), the shrine building was burned down in the course of the attack led by {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en|Oda Nobunaga|qid=Q171411|lt=Oda Nobunaga|1=Oda Nobunaga}} against {{ill|Ishiyama Hongan-ji|en|Ishiyama Hongan-ji|qid=Q1098123|lt=Osaka Hongan-ji|1=Ishiyama Hongan-ji}} ({{ill|Ishiyama Hongan-ji War|en|Ishiyama Hongan-ji War|qid=Q859815|lt=Ishiyama War|1=Ishiyama Hongan-ji War}}).

Subsequently the site of Himekoso Shrine fell into ruin and even the location of its main hall became unknown. However, in the 8th year of the {{ill|Tenmei|en|Tenmei|qid=Q1194121|lt=Tenmei Period|1=Tenmei}} (1788), someone claimed to have discovered ancient sacred treasures of Himekoso Shrine, and based on that the shrine's legend was compiled – assigning the identity of Shikinaisha/Himekoso Shrine to the existing Ushiwatennō Shrine and enshrining {{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|シタテルヒメ|lt=Lower Illumination Hime|lt_ja=下照比売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|qq=}} as its principal deity, with our shrine subsequently changing its name from Ushiwatennō Shrine to Himekoso Shrine, thereby being restored. However, the {{ill|Osaka Prefecture Shrine History Materials|ja|大阪府神社史資料|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka Prefecture Shrine History Materials|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} record that this legend "is not to be trusted."

In 1872 (the 5th year of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}}), it was classified as a {{ill|Mura-sha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度}}.
